newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo boosts education spending.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo boosts education spending.

text.p: Mexico's President Ernesto Zedillo announced higher education spending for 1997 on Tuesday, saying it was the best way to fight poverty and underdevelopment.
The government has earmarked 188 billion pesos ($24 billion) for spending on education this year, a real increase of 7.2 percent over 1996, Zedillo said.
The budget would consolidate the "heroic educational feat" that has raised Mexicans' average years of schooling by 650 percent over the last 75 years, he said.
"Education is the best item on which the people of Mexico can spend their money," Zedillo said. "This amount is one-quarter of all budgeted spending, and 43 percent of all social spending."
Zedillo said funds would be channelled into more deprived regions and Indian communities.
He said the average Mexican had 7.2 years of education in 1995, compared to just one year in 1920.
